hardware_architecture.description: Puppy defines MDBP (Most Direct Binary Path) for all hardware
hardware_architecture.key_principle: Each hardware component has its own SUB-PROCESSOR that directs signal flow - binaries (SXF) carry the actual type logic, not just data
hardware_architecture.signal_flow: Signal flows through rails to specialized sub-processors, NOT to main CPU/GPU/NPU as primary target
hardware_architecture.main_processors_role: CPU/GPU/NPU are HEAVY-LIFT FALLBACKS - not primary execution targets
hardware_architecture.sub_processors: Each rail (graphicsrail, nicrails, etc.) contains primitive processors that execute binary logic locally
hardware_architecture.binary_execution: SXF (Sara Executable Format) carries the actual computational logic that runs on sub-processors

deflection_circuits.description: Hardware-level circuits that route/deflect based on BINARY signals - NOT processors, but binary-controlled switches
deflection_circuits.historical_note: These existed in 286-era and prior, many now in sockets not chips - SLAM accounts for them

circuit_types.purpose: Wake-on-LAN auxiliary rail - standby power routing

deflection_circuits.example_in_nicrails: nicrails.slam contains SerDes, PLL, WOL, RF, Antenna Switch, BT Coex circuits

runtime_architecture.processor_units: hw_cpu defined in MDBP across all SLAM files
runtime_architecture.binary_format: SXF - Sara Executable Format (9 blocks defined)
runtime_architecture.status: SPEC_DEFINED - implementation pending for binary SXF execution
what_is_defined: All runtime flow: puppy → dogtag → collar → latch → lead → handle → post
what_needs_implementation: SXF binary loader - reads SXF blocks from storage/memory
SXF execution engine - executes binary operations on sub-processors
Hardware bridge - connects SXF execution to rail deflection circuits
